chapter: Old styles, big bands and rhythm sections
title: Desert island picks: Wes, Armstrong, Benny Carter
summary: He chooses Wes Montgomery, Armstrong records and Carter's 'Further Definitions'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What’s on your desert island playlist?

Ah the old desert island. I should always think about that more, because, and of course it changes all the time I mean. Of course I’d have to have a Wes Montgomery record, and as to what my favorite one is it’s kind of hard to say because I like all of them. Even the Creed Taylor stuff that he did later with the “California Dreamin’” and that stuff. Probably if I had to pick one I’d probably pick “The Incredible Jazz Guitar” Wes Montgomery. That’s what everybody says is probably the best one. I’d have to have some Armstrong, I don’t even know which album for that. I guess I would just pick a 78 maybe and one of my favorites of his was — well there are two — his big band version of “Struttin’ with Some Barbeque,” it’s fantastic, the Decca version of that, it’s oh my God. And also “Wolverine Blues” that he does later with Sid Catlett playing drums behind him man. That’s a kick-ass record. So both of them, I would take one or the other. I had another one just on the tip of my tongue. Oh, we listened to it last night, I would take Benny Carter’s “Further Definitions” album with me. That is a great record. It’s only

about 35 minutes long but it’s great. I mean there’s not a track on there where you’re waiting for it to get over to get to the next track. Every track is perfect. I just love that record. So I guess those are enough.
